summary.intent: Investigate and fix E2E test failures on PR #449 (fix/desktop-e2e-sequence-mismatch), tracing failures introduced by PR #448's IPNS publish/signature changes and a pre-existing FUSE desktop upload drain bug.
summary.outcome: Web E2E tests fixed (175/176 passing, 1 remaining flaky Sapphire login) by making IPNS signature verification non-fatal and fixing deprecated protobuf wire type handling. Desktop E2E partially fixed — inode-not-found bug resolved and FUSE drain added to readdir, but macOS still failing due to SMB cache preventing ls from reaching FUSE layer. Session ends mid-fix.

repo: PR #448 changed apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts and apps/api/src/ipns/ipns-record-parser.ts to add publicKey on publish and signature verification on resolve — this broke vault initialization across all multi-account web E2E tests.
The 91 skipped tests in web E2E are all cascade failures from 5 setup failures (invite-link, writable-shares, mfa-flows, media-preview, recovery suites) — actual unique root causes are far fewer.
Desktop E2E failures pre-date PR #448; they began with PR #446 around April 2 and are a separate FUSE pipeline issue.
macOS FUSE-T uses an SMB backend that caches directory listings — ls may not reach the FUSE layer, so readdir drain doesn't trigger reliably.

Windows dir_ops.rs already had drain_upload_completions() in its readdir handler; macOS/Linux did not — an asymmetry that caused the upload pipeline to stall in CI where no background OS events trigger FUSE callbacks.
The Sapphire Devnet 'Error occurred while getting current epoch' alert on the login page is a known flaky env issue unrelated to code bugs.
vault.service.ts duplicate key errors (UQ_folder_ipns_user_ipns) during vault init are expected and already caught — not a root cause.
CI Web E2E was green through April 2, broke April 4 after PR #448 merged.

code.finding: Hard-throwing signature verification on resolve crashed vault init/folder loading. Fixed by wrapping in try/catch, returning signatureVerified: false on failure instead of throwing.
Threw 'Unsupported wire type 4' for deprecated protobuf group types (3=start group, 4=end group), causing delegated routing resolve to fail and fall back to DB cache. Fixed to skip gracefully.
Test expected a throw on wire type 3; updated to verify deprecated group types are skipped instead.

rmdir did not clean up the publish_queue for the deleted inode, causing 'Folder inode not found' errors when the flush attempted to publish a deleted directory. Fixed by removing the inode from publish_queue on rmdir and rename-over-destination.

macOS/Linux readdir handler was missing drain_upload_completions() call present in Windows equivalent — upload completions never processed in CI where no background OS FUSE events occur after file write.
FilePointer polling was 12 attempts x 5s = 60s. Doubled to 24 attempts. Also added ls and repeated FUSE touches inside polling loop to force drain_upload_completions to fire.
Same rmdir/rename publish_queue cleanup fix applied to Windows write_ops for parity.

workflow: Always run pnpm build for all packages (not just @cipherbox/crypto) before starting dev servers to avoid missing built outputs.
When E2E failures look high, separate cascade skips from unique root causes before diagnosing — the actual failure count can be much smaller.
CI Playwright reports can be downloaded as artifacts (gh run download) for detailed error-context.md and screenshot inspection without re-running tests locally.
Checking git log against CI run timestamps is an effective way to pinpoint which PR introduced a regression.
Rust fuse module: after release() spawns a background upload, no further FUSE callbacks are guaranteed in CI headless environments — drain must be triggered explicitly.

friction: Local dev environment was down (PostgreSQL/Redis at 192.168.133.12 unreachable) for much of the session, blocking local E2E re-runs and forcing reliance on CI for validation.
GitHub CLI OAuth token expired mid-session, blocking CI log queries.
Playwright output buffering made it hard to track test progress in real-time.
macOS FUSE-T SMB caching meant ls didn't reliably reach the FUSE layer, requiring repeated touch-based workarounds.
Long round-trip of commit → push → CI trigger → wait → analyze added significant latency to each fix iteration.
The 'Error occurred while getting current epoch' Sapphire error was a red herring that consumed investigation time before being ruled out.
open_items: macOS desktop E2E still failing at end of session — the repeated FUSE touch approach in the polling loop was committed but CI result not yet confirmed.
recovery.spec.ts skipped entirely — IPNS mock routing 404 (POST /api/v0/name/resolve) causing empty progress log; root cause not investigated.
The 1 remaining flaky web E2E failure (batch-download or media-preview wallet login timeout) is attributed to Sapphire Devnet instability but not definitively confirmed or fixed.
Windows desktop E2E was passing but the PowerShell polling script changes were made speculatively — should verify Windows CI stays green.

The FUSE drain architecture asymmetry between Windows and macOS/Linux was patched reactively; a more systematic audit of drain_upload_completions call sites across all platform impls may be warranted.
PR #449 was originally about desktop-e2e-sequence-mismatch but grew to include web IPNS fixes and FUSE drain fixes — PR scope has expanded significantly from its original intent.
